correctness.rationale: For every finite tree the oriented edge first-passage identity and commute identity hold exactly. Every path ancestor has at most the longest second-predecessor run plus one earlier-side bypass labels, giving a pathwise O(N log N) error versus twice the sum of path labels. Backward ancestry yields a joint inverse-renewal count/integral representation with iid {1,2} increments. Donsker inversion and Brownian integral covariance 1/3, cross-covariance 1/6 prove the displayed bivariate Gaussian law. Hoeffding and Borel--Cantelli prove the leading almost-sure laws. The packaged verifier passed 4,898,253 deterministic assertions, including all histories through N=12 and independent exact linear-system hitting times through N=7; finite tests do not establish the weak limit.

value.rationale: The source paper identifies infinite collision without quantifying how random geometry controls directed search costs. The new theorem gives the complete joint Gaussian limit for the most natural oldest/newest first-passage conditional means, their sharp N^2 cost and N^{3/2} random-geometry fluctuation scales, and the unexpected universal cross-correlation 1/2 at every nondegenerate attachment probability. This is an interpretable, nontrivial bivariate invariant of the Bernoulli recursive-tree model rather than a routine renaming, a single small instance, or a table recomputation.
